alex-ae: FYI - large PLG customer asked for a short POC: ingest their legal & product docs, answer long-form questions, and run workflow tool calls (create calendar invites / redact PHI). Asked for success criteria and estimated cost. Can SEs weigh in?
tara-se: I can take lead on technical scoping. Quick clarifying q: what max context do they need? they mentioned whole contracts + chat history.
alex-ae: They said ~30k tokens per doc in worst case, frequent multi-doc queries. Also want reranking for retrieval and embeddings for search.
samir-se: Ok that points to a model with >=32k context. Candidate: `redwood-4-32k` for generation + `redwood-embed-14` for embeddings. Reranker could be a small cross-encoder or an MLP over embeddings depending on latency.
tara-se: For tool calling, we need to support structured tool outputs (invite JSON) + a safe redaction step before returning. We'll prototype with function-calling and a middleware that runs a PII-detect model.
maria-sec: Security checklist: they require EU data residency, KMS integration, and SOC2 evidence. Also asked about in-flight request logging retention and ability to disable logging for specific routes.
jon-pm: Timeline constraints: they want 4-week POC, with a demo at week 3. Success criteria from sales: (1) end-to-end ingest -> retrieval -> answer accuracy >= 85% on their eval set, (2) <=600ms median response for single-doc short queries and <=1200ms for multi-doc aggregated queries, (3) tool calls executed and audited, (4) data residency + KMS confirmed.
samir-se: On accuracy we should lock down evals early. Ask customer for 50 representative queries + ground truth answers. We can run A/B between `redwood-4-32k` and `redwood-3-16k` (with chunking) to measure quality vs cost.
tara-se: For throughput/cost estimates: rough per-token compute for 32k model is ~2.5x the 16k variant. If they plan heavy long-context usage, recommend dedicated capacity reservation to control latency and cost.
alex-ae: Pricing question came up: do we have a standard dedicated POC rate or should we build a custom estimate? Customer expects a capped-month cost.
jon-pm: We typically offer a short-term reserved bundle for POCs: 1 GPU pool + support at a discounted commit. Sales can propose a capped usage estimate. I'll draft numbers once SEs give token/req estimates.
maria-sec: For logging, we can support route-level logging disable and KMS-managed envelope encryption. Will need security questionnaire answers for the SOC2 attestation — I can pull the standard pack but check EU residency options.
samir-se: Action items for SEs: 1) define ingest pipeline (formatting, chunking, embeddings index), 2) design eval harness (50 queries + metric script), 3) perf run plan (1k synthetic multi-doc queries), 4) tool-calling prototype with redaction. ETA 5 business days for a first draft.
tara-se: On model selection note: if some queries only need short context we can route them to `redwood-3-16k` to save cost. We'll need routing policy: by query length + cost budget per request. Could demo fallback routing during POC.
alex-ae: Customer also asked about offline rerank batch jobs to precompute top-k for common queries. Feasible?
samir-se: Yes — we can precompute embeddings + nearest neighbors daily, then run a lightweight neural reranker at query time. That reduces latency vs on-the-fly rerank for heavy queries.
maria-sec: One blocker: customer insists on HSM-backed key storage. We support KMS integrations; need docs for supported HSMs and an architect call if they require on-prem HSM.
jon-pm: I'll schedule the joint kickoff next Tue. Alex — confirm customer can provide the 50 eval queries by then.
alex-ae: I'll ask for evals and sample docs today. Also will confirm their expected monthly QPS to size dedicated pool.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: created ticket INF-POC-231 for POC infra requests, assigned to eng-ops.
samir-se: I'll start drafting the POC runbook and include cost scenarios (hosted vs dedicated). Will post draft in this thread when ready.
tara-se: If we can get the eval set this week, we can have A/B results by week 2 which helps sales pricing call.
alex-ae: Great — thanks everyone. I'll loop in legal for data processing agreement once security confirms KMS/residency.
maria-sec: I'll attach SOC2 + KMS docs and note any gaps. Expect those in the thread later today.
